palette.border_role: Card borders, input fields, dividers, property card edges

redfin_header_case_study.what: Original Redfin header used brand-red as background color across the entire header
redfin_header_case_study.why_bad: Red background overwhelmed page content, required bright orange buttons to stand out, felt 'jarring and untrustworthy'
redfin_header_case_study.fix: Switched header background to white — engagement with every page increased over 500%
redfin_header_case_study.lesson: Brand color should accent, not dominate. White headers let content breathe. Red specifically signals danger/stop when overused.

redfin_navigation_case_study.what: Original nav had no inclusion criteria — any link could land in the header causing duplicates and poor hierarchy
redfin_navigation_case_study.why_bad: Low-value pages stole clicks from higher-priority destinations, visual clutter overwhelmed users
redfin_navigation_case_study.fix: Single-row header with clear Buy vs Sell separation — Buy page views rose 338%, inquiry form submissions increased 285%
redfin_navigation_case_study.lesson: Ruthlessly prioritize navigation. Separate buyer and seller journeys. Test incrementally — A/B tests reached significance in <1 week due to high traffic.

redfin_mobile_case_study.what: 90% of mobile users tapped the logo to go home regardless of what the button label said
redfin_mobile_case_study.why_bad: Traditional hamburger menu was ignored; users developed their own navigation heuristic
redfin_mobile_case_study.fix: Simplified to 3 items: Home Buying, Selling, App upsell; replaced hamburger with simple dropdown arrow
redfin_mobile_case_study.lesson: Observe actual user behavior, not intended behavior. The logo is the universal 'take me home' button on mobile.
